content: If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store the medication at room temperature, away from moisture. Do not open the packets until you are ready to use the medication. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. Esomeprazole is used to treat certain stomach and esophagus conditions, such as acid reflux and ulcers. It works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, relieving symptoms like heartburn, difficulty swallowing, and persistent cough. This medication also helps heal acid-related damage to the stomach and esophagus, prevents ulcers, and may reduce the risk of esophageal cancer. Before starting esomeprazole, read the Medication Guide and any Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication by mouth as directed by your doctor, usually once daily, at least one hour before a meal. It may also be administered through a nasogastric or gastric tube if necessary. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. For 5-milligram strength packets, mix the contents with one teaspoon (5 milliliters) of water, stir well, and let it sit for 2 to 3 minutes to thicken. Stir again and drink the mixture within 30 minutes. For other strengths, mix the packet contents with one tablespoon (15 milliliters) of water, stir, let it sit for 2 to 3 minutes, stir again, and drink within 30 minutes. Do not crush or chew the granules. Antacids may be taken alongside this medication if needed. Use this medication regularly for the best results, and take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Inform your doctor if your condition persists or worsens. Be aware that the risk of side effects may increase over time. Common side effects include headache and abdominal pain. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, esomeprazole may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacterial infection (Clostridium difficile), which can occur during or after treatment. Long-term use of proton pump inhibitors like esomeprazole may lead to vitamin B-12 deficiency, especially if taken daily for three years or longer. Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, such as bone loss and fractures. Before taking esomeprazole, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other proton pump inhibitors (e.g., omeprazole, lansoprazole), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Some symptoms may indicate a more serious condition. Proton pump inhibitors may increase the risk of bone fractures, particularly with prolonged use, higher doses, and in older adults. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if esomeprazole passes into breast milk, but similar drugs do. The effects on a nursing infant are not well understood. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some medications require stomach acid for proper absorption, and esomeprazole may interfere with their effectiveness. This medication is very similar to omeprazole and may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If your doctor has instructed you to use this medication long-term, periodic lab tests (e.g., magnesium levels, vitamin B-12 levels) may be necessary. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled.
